Hi, Rob:

I tried to define  iter =5000 and warmup=3000 for each chain (4 chains in total) using the following codes. However,according to print() , each chain only with iter=2000; warmup=1000;.

How to  modify iter/warmup for parallel sampling? Any suggestion is appreciated.

Thanks a lot.

Lisa


>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
library(parallel)
library(rstan)

foo_data <- exp1.list.1;
rng_seed <- 1234567;
foo <- stan("exp1.stan", data = foo_data, chains = 0, warmup=3000, iter =5000)

sflist <-  mclapply(1:4, mc.cores = 6, 
         function(i) stan(fit = foo, data = foo_data, 
                          seed = rng_seed, 
                          chains = 1, chain_id = i, 
                           refresh = -1))

fit <- sflist2stanfit(sflist)

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Ask about Sample multiple chains in parallel
parts:
On Thursday, December 11, 2014 3:05:42 PM UTC-5, Lisa Mu wrote:
library(parallel)
library(rstan)

foo_data <- exp1.list.1;
rng_seed <- 1234567;
foo <- stan("exp1.stan", data = foo_data, chains = 0, warmup=3000, iter =5000)

It does not remember the 3000 and 5000, so you need to repeat the warmup and iter when you call stan() below. Also, there is no reason to use 6 cores for only 4 chains, so you could do 4 cores or 6 chains.

sflist <-  mclapply(1:4, mc.cores = 6, 
         function(i) stan(fit = foo, data = foo_data, 
                          seed = rng_seed, 
                          chains = 1, chain_id = i, 
                           refresh = -1))
Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Ask about Sample multiple chains in parallel
parts:
You need to configure the mclapply function for
number of warmup and iterations.

The doc says that "chains = 0" is illegal (it says "positive integer"),
but it seems to work for you, so that looks like a bug in the doc or
in the error checking. I think what you want is iter=0. Or you
can compile the model using stan_model() and then call sampling().

- Bob

Hi, Bob:

I tried either "chains=0" or "iter=0" , although there are warning messages for both , they still can be passed to  mclapply, and gave same results. 

Anyway, they meet my purpose to reduce running time. Please let me know if you have any concern.

Thanks.

Lisa

rng_seed <- 1234567;

foo <- stan("exp1.stan", data = foo_data, chains = 0)
  # the number of chains is less than 1; sampling not done
sflist <- 
 mclapply(1:4, mc.cores = 4,

function(i) stan(fit = foo, data = foo_data, 
                           seed = rng_seed, 
                           chains = 1, chain_id = i,
warmup=3000, iter =5000,

refresh = -1))
